perspective:
**Ethan Mohamud’s available information:**

- I am Ethan Mohamud. Gary Guo is my long-time friend; we met in middle school and have stayed close. Gary is a doctor.
- I noticed Gary was working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- I was concerned about Gary’s health, so I invited him to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- Gary told me he appreciated my concern but said he couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- During the retreat, I observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected his overworking involved more than professional obligations.
- I confronted Gary, telling him we had been friends since middle school, that he could tell me anything, and that I wanted to help, not judge.
- Gary told me it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden me with his problems.
- After that, Gary opened up to me about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- I offered to help by suggesting he prioritize tasks and delegate some responsibilities. Gary agreed that sounded good and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself too.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges.
- Gary told me things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had even had time for a movie the previous weekend. I felt hopeful and proud and encouraged him.
- After a year, I saw that Gary had adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and could manage on his own. I decided to step back while letting him know I’m always available if needed.
- I told Gary I was always just a call away and that he had this. Gary thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and said he felt more in control.
